_note: Public template. Copy to axon-overlay/config/scouting.json and fill real values there — never here. Replace <knowledge-base-root> with that deployment's absolute or home-relative knowledge-store path before enabling either Obsidian source. scouting resolves config from $SJEL_PERSONAL_ROOT/config/scouting.json at runtime (see src/config.rs Config::load). Every field is optional; the tool runs against empty/local dirs with zero config.
_comment_interest_profile: Directory of markdown files describing what you're interested in (one file per focus area). Convention: 'summary:' / 'current_focus:' frontmatter lines plus a '> [!quote] Charter' blockquote paragraph — score.rs parses this generically, it does not have to be an Obsidian vault. A file named exactly 'Focus.md' is treated as a hub/lens and skipped, not scored. Superseded by source entries with profiles_glob.
_comment_events: Directory of existing markdown event notes to cross-reference newly discovered opportunities against (annotate-only — never written to). Leave unset to skip this entirely. Superseded by source entries with events_glob.
_comment_embeddings: Optional pre-computed opportunity-embeddings JSON (see README). Left as a --opp-embeddings CLI flag in practice; set here only if you always want the same file.
_comment_embedding_backend: Nothing about embedding lives in this file. Interest-profile vectors come from the 'embedding' role in the overlay's inference.json (backend, model, query/document prefixes), read through libs/inference; a machine that declares no such role falls back to hash embedding. See libs/inference/README.md and src/embed.rs.
_comment_sources: Declared opportunity sources (supersedes events_dir/interest_profile_dir). Each entry declares an adapter type and location. The pipeline runs all enabled sources when no --adapter flag is given. See capabilities/scouting/README.md.
_comment_data_class: data_class declares what a source's opportunities are worth protecting: c0 public, c1 mine, c2 others, c3 secret (PRD Axon.md §6.1). GET /opportunities publishes it on every row and GET /sources publishes each declaration. OMITTING IT IS SAFE AND MEANS c1: the class is never guessed, and c0 is reachable only by saying so — the same rule comms applies to its feed sources. A value outside c0..c3 is refused down to c1 and reported at load, because a typo must not be more permissive than silence. Every hardcoded adapter (luma, meetup, cfp, euro_hackathons, transit_fare) has no entry here and is therefore c1.
_comment_profile_path: profiles_glob resolves under 'path' by default — the form every entry used before 'profile_path' existed, still working unchanged. Declare 'profile_path' when the matching profile does not belong in the store the opportunities come from: a profile is a consumer input, your own predicate about what is worth surfacing, and the two systems have separate sync lifecycles. Either way the read stays bounded by whichever root declared it; a glob climbing out with '..' is refused rather than followed.

sources._comment: The split form: opportunities come out of the knowledge store, the profile scoring them lives wherever this deployment keeps its own profile state. Same source id, same stable opportunity ids — only where the predicate is read from changes.

One tracked Luma calendar. 'url' is the calendar's cal-… api id, NOT a lu.ma slug — Luma publishes no public slug→id lookup, so the adapter rejects a slug rather than building a URL that 404s. Read the id off any event: `scout --emit-json --adapter luma --location berlin` and look at raw.calendar_api_id. The id below is the public Claude Community Events calendar.
sources._comment_splash: One Splash That brand event hub. Splash is white-label, so this one adapter covers every brand hosting there; 'url' is '<host>/<hub_id>', because the query is same-origin and the numeric id alone does not say which host answers for it. Find the id in the hub page's own XHR (the splash_hub_id parameter) — an event page does not carry it, and a slug is refused rather than guessed at. The adapter always asks for upcoming events: unfiltered, a hub returns its entire history, which for the one this was built against is 3015 records and 5.5 MB.

sources._comment_data_class: A public event hub, fetched anonymously: no session of the operator's decides what it returns, which is the argument comms already makes for the GitHub Trending page. The obsidian-markdown entries above deliberately declare nothing — a note in a knowledge store is the operator's, and c1 is what silence already means.

_comment_sources_example_rss: You can also use RSS/Atom feeds as event sources. The RSS adapter does a lightweight parse (no XML crate dependency).

_comment_calendar_base_url: Base URL of capabilities/calendar for `scout --promote-calendar`. Loopback only — calendar binds through libs/axon-server's serve_local. Defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8087, calendar's own default port.
_comment_home_timezone: Your home timezone, used to turn Luma's UTC instants into the naive local wall time calendar stores. DECLARE IT ONCE, in the overlay's config/deployment.env as SJEL_HOME_TIMEZONE (schemas/deployment.env.example) — calendar needs the same value, and two independent copies agree until one is edited. Setting it here still overrides, but a value that disagrees with the deployment declaration is an error naming both files. NO DEFAULT either way: promoting without one would silently write the wrong hour, so --promote-calendar refuses until it resolves (or --timezone is passed). Accepts UTC, a fixed ±HH:MM offset, or one of the supported IANA zones listed in src/localtime.rs.
_comment_geo: Private routing policy for physical events. Set home_latitude, home_longitude, and local_radius_km together in the overlay to classify complete coordinate pairs by great-circle distance; there are deliberately no public home or radius defaults. Sparse events fall back to the local country tokens and then timezone prefixes. allow_unknown=true is an explicit compatibility override; false leaves evidence-free events unresolved. No route drops an opportunity.
